newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Poll sees Singapore exports down 4.5 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Poll sees Singapore exports down 4.5 pct in March.

text.p: Singapore industry has still not recovered from a slump in the island's key electronics sector, a Reuters poll suggested on Thursday.
A survey of 11 economists from local financial institutions produced an average forecast of a drop of 4.5 percent year-on-year in the country's non-oil domestic exports in March in nominal terms.
This compares with a fall of 7.9 percent in February and a drop of 3.1 percent in January.

"Exports had still not recovered in March," said Prasenjit Basu, regional economist at Union Bank of Switzerland. "But they were not as weak as they were in February and the momentum of output seems to have been picking up slowly."
The Reuters survey was uniformly negative, with one pessimist going for a decline of around 10.6 percent year-on-year and even the most optimistic economist predicting a fall of 1.7 percent.
It was the first Reuters survey in Singapore to include no positive forecasts for monthly export figures since polling began in mid-1996.
Singapore has traditionally had a vibrant export-oriented manufacturing sector which in recent years has concentrated on the high-technology end of the electronics industry.
Electronics, computer parts and related products account for about half the country's industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
The island's non-oil exports were worth a total of Singapore $5.52 billion (US$3.83 billion) in nominal terms in February.

But a slowdown in demand for personal computers last year and a consequent overhang of inventory in the electronics industry, particularly in the United States, led to a fall in demand for electronics components, hitting Asian producers.

Since the third quarter of last year, Singapore exports have reflected slower sales of electronics products and this slump has also been passed into some other sectors of the economy related to the manufacturing sector.

Most economists believe the current slump will end in the second half of this year but say the scale of the current slowdown has been underestimated in the past by economists and also by the government.
"There is still underlying weakness in the electronics industry." said Kaan Quan Hon, head of economics at the research arm of the Development Bank of Singapore.
Seema Desai, Southeast Asian regional economist at Schroders in Singapore, said the consensus on Singapore's economic recovery had been too optimistic in recent months.
"We are expecting some sort of recovery in the next few months, but we think it will be very mild," she said.

"There are already signs that some electronics companies are moving production out of Singapore to cheaper locations and we just don't see the PC (personal computer) market recovering back to its buoyant 1996 levels."

Desai predicts Singapore's gross domestic product will grow by 5.7 percent in 1997, down from seven percent in 1996, 8.8 percent in 1995 and a double-digit expansion in the previous two years. Most other economists suggest GDP growth will be closer to seven percent this year.
Singapore's Trade Development Board is expected to publish official export data for March on April 21.
